title: Only Mark moves work across the interactive boundary: fleet_dash's user key or a one-shot grant from his typed command

story.i_want_to: be the only one who moves an item between my interactive session and the loop, by fleet_dash or by typing /work-item-move in that session
story.so_that: work moves in and out of my sessions at my will, never at an agent's whim

rationale: PRD R2: 'A move between one of Mark's interactive sessions and the loop happens only on Mark's explicit act ... fleet_dash, under his user key; a slash command he types ... The harness turns his typed command into a one-shot grant, and the move tool refuses a boundary move without one.' US-52.43's move accepts any :agent-or-higher caller. Signed single-use tokens already exist: capability_tokens with typ, story_id, expires_at, consumed_at and a tenant-key signature (Loopctl.Capabilities.mint/4, verify/2, consume/1, lib/loopctl/capabilities.ex:51,184,210), so the grant is a new token type, not a new mechanism. US-52.40 recorded whether a UserPromptSubmit hook can tell a typed command from every other origin (its grant_rule).

acceptance_criteria.description: Moves.boundary?/2 is true when the item's source holder (its current holder, or for an unheld item the from_holder_id of its last move, else the holder of its last claim) or the move's target holder has kind interactive; a move between a runner session and a host or the loop is not a boundary move.

A boundary move without a valid grant, by any caller other than a :user or :superadmin key that carries no holder_id, is refused before any write with 403 code boundary_move_needs_mark and the message 'Moving work between Mark's session and the loop needs Mark: he types /work-item-move in that session, or moves it from fleet_dash.'
A boundary move by a :user key with no holder_id (fleet_dash) is applied without a grant, and its moved or move_requested event names that key as the actor.

POST /api/v1/move_grants (exact_role: :agent) by an interactive holder's credential with {item, target, prompt_sha256} mints a capability_tokens row of typ move_grant carrying the holder_id, the item's story_id and the target in scope, expiring in 600 s, and answers 201 {grant}; a runner_session or cloud holder, or a key with no holder, is refused 403 code grant_needs_interactive_session, and an item that resolves to no story of the tenant 404 item_not_found.

A move carrying a grant is applied only when the grant verifies (tenant signature, typ move_grant, unexpired), its holder is the move's source or target holder, and its story and target equal the move's; the grant is consumed in the move's transaction; a reused grant is refused 409 code grant_replayed, a mismatch 403 grant_mismatch and an expired one 403 grant_expired.

factory/hooks/work-item-move-grant.sh, run on UserPromptSubmit, mints a grant only when the prompt's first token is exactly /work-item-move followed by an item and a target (loop, here, host:<name> or session:<holder_id>, with here meaning this session's holder), and prints the grant id as additional context; any other prompt prints nothing; every path exits 0 within 3 s, and a failed mint prints 'No move grant was minted: <reason>.'

factory/commands/work-item-move.md tells the session to call work_item_move with the typed item and target and the grant from its context, and to call nothing when the context says no grant was minted.

work_item_move accepts grant and its description names boundary_move_needs_mark, grant_replayed, grant_mismatch and grant_expired; mcp-server/test/route_coverage.test.js lists POST /api/v1/move_grants as exempt because its caller is the hook, never a session's tool call.

e2e/test/two_sessions_one_repo_test.exs (US-52.20) gains two steps on session A's item: session B's work_item_checkpoint is refused not_holder (US-52.41) and B's work_item_move to loop is refused 403 boundary_move_needs_mark (AC-52.45.2), and A's item is unchanged after both (same claim_epoch, holder and newest checkpoint).

technical_notes: Grant storage is capability_tokens (lib/loopctl/capabilities/capability_token.ex:12-23): add move_grant to @types, a nullable holder_id (FK holders) and a scope jsonb; mint through a Capabilities.mint_move_grant/4 beside mint/4 (capabilities.ex:51) so the signature check on mint is shared; verify/2 and consume/1 (:184, :210) are reused, consume running inside the move transaction.

The hook is the only minting caller: claude-config hooks already call loopctl with curl and a key from the environment (hooks/kb-recall-on-prompt.sh:191-192,306), and a session's own Bash curl to loopctl is refused by claude-config's hooks/orchestrator-guardrail.sh, so an agent reaches the mint only by bypassing its own guards. The grant defends against an agent's whim, as R2 asks, not against a session that disables its harness.

The hook presents the session's holder credential from $HOME/.claude/loopctl-holders/<session_id>.key, the mode-0600 file the MCP server writes on register and rotation (US-52.28 AC-52.28.1), choosing the file by the session_id in its stdin JSON; no file means no grant and the no-grant line. A headless runner session is a runner_session holder, so even if `claude -p` fires the hook (US-52.40's probe) its mint is refused by AC-52.45.4.
Item reference: a story uuid, or <owner/repo>#<issue> resolved through the tenant's intake records (Loopctl.Intake; the intake record links a story to its issue, PRD section 3 concept 1).

factory/ is this repo's home for harness parts until release 8's factory pack packages them (README names table gains factory/hooks and factory/commands); until then claude-config registers the hook path and the command in its settings, one claude-config change in this release.

If docs/factory/measurements/release-7.md says grant_rule: fleet_dash_only, AC-52.45.4 to AC-52.45.7 are not built, AC-52.45.2's message drops its first path, and the story's report says so (defaults).
Boundary check placement: Moves.move/4 (US-52.43) before any write; the deadline worker and Moves.place_pending/2 act on moves already admitted and do not re-check.
non_goals: Pulling into an interactive session and its ad-hoc items: US-52.46.
fleet_dash's own move control: fleet_dash is another repo; it calls POST /api/v1/stories/:id/move with Mark's user key.
Defending against a session that removes its own hooks: out of scope by PRD R2's own terms.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.45.6: when the hook cannot reach loopctl within its timeout no grant exists, the prompt proceeds, and the move is refused rather than applied without Mark.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.45.4: the grant is a capability_tokens row in loopctl's Postgres, signed by the tenant key; the session's context only carries its id.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.45.5: a grant is consumed in the move's transaction, so a retried move with the same move_id answers the first result (US-52.43) and a second move with the same grant is grant_replayed.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.45.6: the hook's mint is bounded at 3 s so a slow loopctl never stalls Mark's prompt; the grant's 600 s life covers a slow agent turn.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.45.3: fleet_dash reaches the move route by item id from anywhere; the hook runs inside the session that typed the command.

defaults: Command: /work-item-move <item> <target>; targets loop, here, host:<name>, session:<holder_id>.
If US-52.40 recorded grant_rule: fleet_dash_only, only the user-key path is built.
definition_of_done: In an interactive session on minis with the hook registered: typing `/work-item-move <sandbox item> loop` leaves a capability_tokens row with consumed_at set, and the same work_item_move call made by the agent unprompted is refused 403 boundary_move_needs_mark.
